questions.q: Why does DMS read the source database's transaction log for CDC instead of periodically running SELECT queries to detect changes?
options: The transaction log captures every committed change in order with minimal load on the source, unlike repeated polling queries against production
SELECT queries are technically impossible against a live database
The transaction log is faster to query than a table but shows the same information a poll would
DMS is physically incapable of running SQL queries
questions.explain: Reading the transaction log lets DMS see every committed change without adding repeated query load to the production source — the same mechanism the database uses internally for recovery and replication.

questions.q: What does the combined "Migrate existing data and replicate ongoing changes" migration type do?
options: Performs a full load, then applies every change from the log position noted at the start of the full load, with no gap
Only replicates changes, skipping the initial data entirely
Runs the full load and CDC simultaneously on unrelated tables
Requires a completely separate DMS task for CDC to begin
questions.explain: DMS notes the transaction log position when the full load starts, then continuously applies changes from that exact position once the full load finishes, avoiding gaps or duplicate application.

questions.q: For SQL Server as a CDC source, what does DMS read to capture ongoing changes?
options: The SQL Server transaction log
A nightly full table export
The Windows Event Log
Application-level audit tables the developer must build manually
questions.explain: DMS reads SQL Server's transaction log (with CDC or replication enabled on the source) to capture changes, analogous to binlog for MySQL and redo logs for Oracle.

questions.q: What is a realistic use case this lesson gives for full load + CDC?
options: Keeping a Redshift warehouse continuously in sync with a live OLTP application database, without analytics queries hitting production directly
One-time archival of a database that will never be queried again
Replacing IAM authentication for RDS
Compressing S3 objects after they're written
questions.explain: A common pattern is using DMS to replicate an OLTP source into a warehouse continuously, so reporting workloads don't compete with the production application for database resources.

questions.q: What does CDC add on top of a plain full load?
options: Ongoing replication of inserts, updates, and deletes made to the source after the initial load completes
Faster initial table copy speed
Automatic schema conversion between different database engines
The ability to migrate without a replication instance
questions.explain: A full load alone is a one-time point-in-time copy; CDC is what keeps the target continuously current with changes made after that copy finished.
